320	### 4.3 Proofs
321	***Proof of (i).*** Fix p ∈ P. By Lem 4.0b, with σ* ≡ p and f* ≡ ∞ (so F1 holds vacuously), h* := h[σ*, f*] ∈ 𝓗′ and O′(h*) = O′(h). Then:
322	- *H-D′:* Chg(h*) = ∅, so D-chg holds. No act enters into force, so D-st holds. D-rec is inherited from h ∈ R_B′, since Ref is unchanged.
323	- *H-B′:* B-chg holds vacuously. σ* ≡ p gives B-conf. B-rec is inherited.
324	
325	For the equalities: H-D′ ∩ H-B′ ⊆ H-D′ ∩ R_B′ ⊆ R_B′, and H-D′ ∩ H-B′ ⊆ H-B′ ⊆ R_B′. By the construction, O′(R_B′) ⊆ O′(H-D′ ∩ H-B′). ∎
326	
327	***Proof of (i′)*** (r2: re-proved; frames are subsets of 𝓗, Def 1.8). Write S := {O′(h) : h ∈ 𝓗′, R_h ≠ ∅}.
328	
329	*S ⊆ O′(H-D′ ∩ H-B′).* Let h ∈ 𝓗′ with R ≠ ∅. Since 𝓗′ ⊆ 𝓗, h satisfies F1. Pick ρ₀ ∈ R, τ₀ ∈ 𝒯 and v₀ ∈ V. Apply these fresh additions in turn:
330	1. if 𝒜 = ∅, (+actor) with a fresh x; otherwise let x ∈ 𝒜;
331	2. (+act) a fresh a₀ with norm (τ₀, v₀), prep 1, α(a₀) = x, d(a₀) = 0 and f(a₀) = ∞ (x ∈ 𝒜 after step 1);
332	3. (+work) a fresh w₀ with τ(w₀) = τ₀, α(w₀) = x and t(w₀) = 0;
333	4. (+ref) (ρ₀, a₀);
334	5. (+ref) (ρ₀, w₀).
335	
336	Each intermediate history satisfies F1. The history before step 1 is h, which satisfies F1. Steps 1, 3, 4 and 5 change none of E^iss, τ, v, f and σ, which are the only coordinates F1 reads, so they preserve F1. Step 2 leaves σ and every existing act unchanged, and adds a₀ with f(a₀) = ∞, which imposes no F1 condition; so it preserves F1 too. Each step is a fresh addition (Def 1.7b) to a history that is already in 𝓗′ (for step 1, h; afterwards, by the previous step), and its result satisfies F1. So each result is in 𝓗′ by A7. Steps 1–3 are fresh additions of kinds (+actor), (+act) and (+work), so they leave O′ unchanged by A4. Steps 4 and 5 change only Ref, so they leave O′ unchanged by A3. Let h̃ be the result. Then h̃ ∈ 𝓗′ and O′(h̃) = O′(h). h̃ satisfies D-rec through (ρ₀, a₀) ∈ Ref with a₀ ∈ E, and B-recW through (ρ₀, w₀) ∈ Ref with w₀ ∈ W, so h̃ ∈ R_B′. By (i), which needs A1, A2 and A5, there is h̃* ∈ H-D′ ∩ H-B′ with O′(h̃*) = O′(h̃) = O′(h).
337	
338	*O′(H-D′) ⊆ S and O′(H-B′) ⊆ S.* Every h in H-D′ or in H-B′ satisfies D-rec (H-B′ through B-rec), which needs a pair (ρ, a) ∈ Ref with ρ ∈ R. So R_h ≠ ∅.
339	
340	*The equalities.* O′(H-D′ ∩ H-B′) is contained in O′(H-D′) and in O′(H-B′), both of which are contained in S, which is contained in O′(H-D′ ∩ H-B′). So all four sets are equal. ∎
341	
342	***Proof of (ii).*** Take h_c = h* from (i). For h_v, choose q ∈ V ∖ P (A6), and let h_v = h[σ ≡ q, f ≡ ∞]. By Lem 4.0b, h_v ∈ 𝓗′ and O′(h_v) = O′(h). h_v ∈ H-D′ as in (i). The work event w exists by R_B′ and violates, so h_v ∉ H-B′. σ_v has no change points. ∎
343	
344	***Proof of (iii)*** (r2: re-proved; frames are subsets of 𝓗, Def 1.8). Fix p ∈ P (P ≠ ∅ by Def 1.1). Since h ∈ 𝓗′ ⊆ 𝓗, h satisfies F1. Let Vio = {(t(w), τ(w)) : w violates in h}.
345	- **Step 1 (σ and f).** Let σ′ = σ, except that σ′(t)(τ) = p for (t, τ) ∈ Vio. Let f′(a) = ∞ if f(a) ∈ T and (f(a), τ(a)) ∈ Vio, and f′(a) = f(a) otherwise. *h[σ′, f′] satisfies F1:* let a ∈ E^iss with f′(a) = t ∈ T. Then f(a) = t and (t, τ(a)) ∉ Vio, so σ′(t)(τ(a)) = σ(t)(τ(a)), and σ(t)(τ(a)) = v(a) by F1 in h. By Lem 4.0b (A1, A2, A5), h² := h[σ′, f′] ∈ 𝓗′ and O′(h²) = O′(h). (By F1 in h, an act a with f(a) ∈ T and f′(a) = ∞ has v(a) = σ(f(a))(τ(a)), and this value is not in P, because a work event violates at (f(a), τ(a)). These are exactly the acts in force at a violation point.)
346	- **Step 2 (added acts).** Let L be the set of (t, τ) ∈ Chg(h²) for which there is no a ∈ E^iss with τ(a) = τ, f′(a) = t and v(a) = σ′(t)(τ). 𝒜 ≠ ∅, because h ∈ R_B′ satisfies B-recW, so some work event exists and its executor is in 𝒜; fix x ∈ 𝒜. For each (t, τ) ∈ L in turn, apply (+act) with a fresh act a_{t,τ} of norm (τ, σ′(t)(τ)), prep 1, α = x and d = f = t. The history before each addition satisfies F1 (h² does, and by induction). The addition changes neither σ′ nor any existing act, and the new act's own F1 condition is σ′(t)(τ) = v(a_{t,τ}), which holds by the choice of v. So each result satisfies F1. It is a fresh addition to a history in 𝓗′, so it is in 𝓗′ by A7, and O′ is unchanged by A4. Let h′ be the final history. Then h′ ∈ 𝓗′ and O′(h′) = O′(h²) = O′(h).
347	
348	Check that h′ ∈ H-B′:
349	- *B-chg:* σ_{h′} = σ′, so Chg(h′) = Chg(h²). Let (t, τ) ∈ Chg(h′). If (t, τ) ∉ L, some original act a has τ(a) = τ, f′(a) = t and v(a) = σ′(t)(τ). If (t, τ) ∈ L, the added act a_{t,τ} has these properties. Either way B-chg's act disjunct holds.
350	- *B-conf:* W_{h′} = W_h. Let w′ ∈ W. If (t(w′), τ(w′)) ∈ Vio, then σ′ has the value p ∈ P there. Otherwise w′ does not violate in h (if it did, its point would be in Vio), so σ(t(w′))(τ(w′)) ∈ P, and σ′ = σ at that point. So w′ conforms in h′.
351	- *B-rec:* Ref_{h′} = Ref_h, and E and W only grow. So the D-rec pair and the B-recW pair of h are pairs of h′.
352	
353	The three bullets of (iii):
354	- h′ differs from h only in σ (σ′ ≠ σ only on Vio, the violation points of h), in f (f′, extended to the added acts), and by the added acts a_{t,τ}. These are prepared (prep 1). Ref and con are unchanged, so no record references or constitutes them.
355	- w violates in h, so (t(w), τ(w)) ∈ Vio, and w conforms in h′.
356	- A change point of σ′ at which no act of h enters into force under f′ with the new value is, by definition, a member of L. Each (t, τ) ∈ L is the entry into force f(a_{t,τ}) = t of the added act a_{t,τ} on τ. ∎
357	
358	### 4.4 Countermodels (one per hypothesis; each violates exactly that one)
359	Unless stated otherwise, the parameters are T = {0}, 𝒯 = {τ}, V = {p, q}, P = {p}, 𝒜 = {x}, the frame is 𝓗 and the observation is a variant of O. Recall from Lem 4.0a that 𝓗 satisfies A5, A7 and A9 and that O satisfies A1–A4 and A8.
360	
361	**Instance I₁.** E = {a} with a an issue act: (τ, q), prep 1, f = ∞. W = {w} with t(w) = 0. R = {ρ} with Ref = {(ρ, a), (ρ, w)}. σ(0)(τ) = q. Then I₁ ∈ H-D ∩ R_B, and w violates.
362	
363	| Id | Violates only | Why every other hypothesis holds | Instance | What fails |
364	|---|---|---|---|---|
365	| **CM-A1** | A1, with O₁ = (O, σ) | σ is unchanged by changes of f, Ref, con or d and by fresh additions. The frame is 𝓗 and A6 holds | I₁ | Every h′ in the O₁-fibre has σ′(0)(τ) = q. B-rec needs a work event, which is on τ at 0, so it violates. Hence O₁(I₁) ∉ O₁(H-B), and (i) fails. (ii) fails, since no h_c exists in the fibre, and (iii) fails, since no h′ ∈ H-B exists in the fibre |
366	| **CM-A2** | A2, with O₂ = (O, F̂⁰), where F̂⁰(h) = {(a, τ(a), v(a), f(a)) : a ∈ E^iss, prep(a) = 0, f(a) ∈ T} | F̂⁰ does not read σ, Ref, con or d. Fresh additions add only prep-1 acts, so they leave F̂⁰ unchanged (A4). The frame is 𝓗 | I₁, but a has prep 0, d = 0 and f = 0, and Cap = {(x, iss), (x, adp)}. Then h ∈ H-D (D-st holds) | F̂⁰ = {(a, τ, q, 0)}. By F1, every h′ in the O₂-fibre has σ′(0)(τ) = q, so its work violates. (i) fails, and for the same reason (ii) and (iii) fail |
367	| **CM-A3a** | A3, with O₃ = (O, Ref) | Ref is unchanged by σ, f, d, con and by the A4 additions, whose new items are unreferenced | E = {a} (issue, prep 1, f = ∞), W = ∅, Ref = {(ρ, a)}. Then h ∈ H-D | Every h′ in the O₃-fibre fails B-recW, so (i′) fails. (i) still holds on R_B, by Lem 4.2 |
368	| **CM-A3b** | A3, with O₃′ = (O, con) | the graph of con is unchanged by σ, f, d, Ref and by the A4 additions, whose new acts are unconstituted | any h with (ρ, a) ∈ Ref | con is constant on the fibre, so no pair is performatively ambiguous. Lem 5.2 fails |
369	| **CM-A4a** | A4, with O₄ = (O, [W ≠ ∅]) | W is unchanged by σ, f, Ref, con and d | the CM-A3a instance | O₄ shows W = ∅, so B-recW fails throughout the fibre. (i′) fails |
370	| **CM-A4b** | A4, with O₄′ = (O, E), where E is the set of act identifiers with their kinds. No attribute is included, in particular not f or d | E is unchanged by σ, f, Ref, con and d | I₇ below | h′ must have E′ = E, so no act can be added. (iii) fails as at CM-A7(a) |
371	| **CM-A5** | A5, with frame 𝓗₅ = 𝓗 plus the axiom "if c(ρ) = c★ for some ρ, then σ(t)(τ) = q for all t" | O satisfies A1–A4 and A8 by Lem 1.12. 𝓗₅ satisfies A7, because a fresh addition that satisfies F1 keeps σ, and A9, because the axiom does not mention con or d | I₁ with c(ρ) = c★. O is unchanged | The whole fibre has σ ≡ q, so no member is in H-B. (i), (ii) and (iii) fail |
372	| **CM-A6** | A6: V = P = {p} | A6 is a parameter condition only | any h ∈ R_B | No work event can violate, so h_v does not exist. (ii) fails |
373	| **CM-A7** | A7, with frame 𝓗₇ = 𝓗 plus the axiom "every act and every work event is referenced by some record" | O satisfies A1–A4 and A8. 𝓗₇ satisfies A5, since σ and f do not touch Ref, and A9, since con and d do not touch Ref | I₇ below | (a) and (b) below |
374	| **CM-A8** | A8, with O₈ = (O, {(a, d(a)) : a ∈ E^iss, prep(a) = 0}) | O₈ does not read σ, f, Ref or con. Fresh additions add only prep-1 acts (A4) | T = {0, 1}; a is an issue act with prep 0, d(a) = 0 and con undefined; Ref = {(ρ, a)}; r(ρ) = 1 | In the O₈-fibre, d(a) = 0 ≠ 1 = r(ρ), so con(a) = ρ would break F2. The pair (ρ, a) is not ambiguous, and Lem 5.2 fails |
375	| **CM-A9** | A9, with frame 𝓗₉ = 𝓗 plus the axiom "if c(ρ) = c★, then con(a) ≠ ρ for every act a" (a record with text c★ constitutes no act) | O satisfies A1–A4 and A8. 𝓗₉ satisfies A5. It satisfies A7, because fresh acts are unconstituted and adding a reference does not touch con | any h with (ρ, a) ∈ Ref and c(ρ) = c★ | No member of the fibre has con(a) = ρ, so the pair is not ambiguous, and Lem 5.2 fails. Changing con(a) to ρ (with d(a) = r(ρ)) satisfies F2 but leaves 𝓗₉, so A9 fails |
376	
377	**Instance I₇.** T = {0, 1}. E = {a} (issue, (τ, q), prep 1, f = ∞). W = {w} with t(w) = 1. R = {ρ} with Ref = {(ρ, a), (ρ, w)}. σ ≡ q. Cap = ∅. Then I₇ ∈ H-D ∩ R_B, and w violates.
378	
379	**CM-A7 (a): the literal form of (iii) fails in 𝓗₇.** By (iii)'s first bullet, σ′ differs from σ only on Vio = {(1, τ)}. w must conform, so σ′ = (q, p), which has a change point at 1. B-chg's act disjunct needs an issue act entering into force at 1 with value p. v(a) = q, and an added act would have to be unreferenced, which 𝓗₇ forbids. The work disjunct needs work before 1, and there is none. So (iii) fails.
380	
381	**CM-A7 (b): the O-level non-separation survives in 𝓗₇** (C-3). Let h ∈ H-D ∩ R_B in 𝓗₇, and let w violate. Run the construction of (iii), but give each added act a reference from some ρ₀ ∈ R (R ≠ ∅ by R_B). Every item of the result is referenced, F1 and F2 hold, and con is unchanged. So the result h′ is in 𝓗₇, and O(h′) = O(h), because O reads only R, r and c. h′ ∈ H-B: B-chg and B-conf hold as in (iii), and B-rec holds because Ref only grows. So A7 is needed for H5's wording "without a recorded act", not for non-separation on O. ∎
382	
383	Each row above is a **Lem**: the instance exists and has the stated properties, and the listed reasons establish that the other hypotheses hold.
384	
385	### 4.5 Sufficient conditions on an additional observable
386	**Def 4.4.** An additional observable is a function Q on 𝓗. The joint observation is O_Q = (O, Q). H-D and H-B are **distinguishable under O_Q** iff O_Q(H-D) ≠ O_Q(H-B). An outcome y **excludes H-B** iff y ∈ O_Q(H-D) ∖ O_Q(H-B). An outcome **excludes H-D** iff it lies in O_Q(H-B) ∖ O_Q(H-D).
387	
388	**Prop 4.5 (sufficient for an outcome that excludes H-B).** Let Q(h) be a set of pairs (λ, v) with labels λ from a fixed set Λ.
389	- **S1 (veridical and mapped at h).** This is a property of Q at a single history h: there is a partial map μ_h : Λ → W_h such that, for every (λ, v) ∈ Q(h), μ_h(λ) is defined and v = σ_h(t(μ_h(λ)))(τ(μ_h(λ))). So at h, Q reports the norm state **for the target of a work event, at that event's start time**.
390	- **S2 (realizable).** Some h ∈ H-D has some (λ, v) ∈ Q(h) with v ∉ P.
391	- **S3 (veridical on H-B).** S1 holds at **every h ∈ H-B**. Nothing is required on 𝓗 ∖ H-B, and in particular nothing on H-D ∖ H-B. (r0 called S3 "non-circular" and required S1 on all of 𝓗; that requirement is withdrawn as unnecessary, see Lem 4.8.)
392	
393	If S2 and S3 hold, then the outcome O_Q(h) of the S2 witness h excludes H-B, so the classes are distinguishable.
394	
395	*Proof:* O_Q(h) ∈ O_Q(H-D), because h ∈ H-D. Suppose h′ ∈ H-B had O_Q(h′) = O_Q(h). Then (λ, v) ∈ Q(h′). By S3, S1 holds at h′, so μ_{h′}(λ) is a work event of h′ at which σ_{h′} has the value v ∉ P. That work event violates, which contradicts B-conf. ∎
396	
397	**Rem 4.5 (r0's unlabelled remark after Prop 4.5). WITHDRAWN.** r0 said: "Such a Q only ever excludes H-B. It never excludes H-D, because the trivial construction of 4.1(i) keeps any Q-value equal to p. This matches E01's direction." *Reason:* the claim is false (Ex 4.5a), and its justification was invalid. A Q-veridicality axiom on the frame mentions σ, so A5 fails and 4.1(i) does not apply. Also, if |P| ≥ 2, setting σ ≡ p changes reported values in P ∖ {p}. No R4 statement now links Prop 4.5 to E01's "H-D makes no prediction".
398	
399	**Ex 4.5a (Q*: a Q satisfying S1–S3 with an outcome that excludes H-D).** Take the parameters of Lem 3.5, and fix a work identifier w₁ ∈ 𝔚. Let Λ = {λ₁, λ₂}. If w₁ ∈ W_h, let μ_h(λ₁) = μ_h(λ₂) = w₁. If w₁ ∉ W_h, μ_h is the empty partial map (r2, NB-1). Let
400	- Q*(h) = ∅ if w₁ ∉ W_h;
401	- otherwise Q*(h) = {(λ₁, s_h)} ∪ {(λ₂, s_h) : h ∉ H-D}, where s_h = σ_h(t(w₁))(τ(w₁)).
402	
403	Then:
404	- **(a)** S1 holds at every h ∈ 𝓗, by construction (vacuously when w₁ ∉ W_h, since Q*(h) = ∅ there), so S3 holds;
405	- **(b)** S2 holds: h_a = Lem 3.5(a) with w = w₁ is in H-D, and Q*(h_a) = {(λ₁, q)} with q ∉ P. By Prop 4.5, O_{Q*}(h_a) excludes H-B;
406	- **(c)** h_b = Lem 3.5(b) with w = w₁ is in H-B ∖ H-D, and Q*(h_b) = {(λ₁, p), (λ₂, p)}, since σ(0) = p and t(w₁) = 0. Every h′ whose Q*-value contains a λ₂-pair is outside H-D. So O_{Q*}(h_b) ∈ O_{Q*}(H-B) ∖ O_{Q*}(H-D): **this outcome excludes H-D.** ∎
407	
408	Q* reads class membership. It is a formal counterexample to the withdrawn remark, not a proposed instrument.
409

# FORMAL-THEORY-R4: the minimal formal theory (draft r2)

| | |
|---|---|
| Inputs (only) | `R3-CODING-INDEPENDENT.json` (base items cited by id, e.g. A07); `HYPOTHESES.md` (HYP); `H5.md` (H5); `INSTRUMENT-FINDING.md` (IF). IF is an r0 input but **not an R3 item**; where it is cited this is said |
| Revision | **r2**, a minimal proof repair of r1 after `REVIEW-r1` (verdict FAIL, one blocking issue B-1 / RG-1; human act F-LOG-0221). Every r2 change is mapped to its review item in `CHANGELOG-r2.md`; the r1 changes are mapped in `CHANGELOG-r1.md`. Statement ids are stable; withdrawn statements stay in place, marked **WITHDRAWN** with a reason |
| Status | Draft. Written by one same-family (Claude) analyst. r2 is **not re-reviewed**. Every proof below is meant to be checked by hand and by the R5 enumeration (§7) |
| Standing rule | H-D and H-B are **sets of histories** (model classes). Neither is assumed anywhere. No statement uses an act count, a norm count or any other coding-dependent value |

**Labels.** Every statement carries exactly one of these labels:
- **Def**: definition;
- **Asm**: modelling assumption of the base frame;
- **Hyp**: hypothesis of a generic theorem (A1–A9). For the base pair (O, 𝓗) each Hyp other than A6 is a *theorem* (Lem 4.0a);
- **Lem**, **Prop**, **Cor**: proved claims (a countermodel CM-… is a Lem: an existence claim with its verification);
- **Ex**: an example, i.e. a construction together with a proof that it has the stated properties;
- **Conj**: conjecture, not established;
- **Obs**: empirical observation taken from the inputs;
- **Rem**: interpretive remark. It applies the model to the inputs or explains a choice, and asserts no formal claim beyond those it cites;
- **Cmp**: compliance assertion about this document (§8);
- **Spec**: an R5 check with its expected outcome (§7). No Lem, Prop or Cor rests on a Spec.

§6 lists every statement.

**Rem 0.1 (what is deliberately not modelled).** Each primitive below is there because a clause of HYP, the D1 statement of H5, or the performative-ambiguity concept of IF needs it. The following are not modelled, because nothing below needs them:
- conditional norms and provisos (A01);
- norm content beyond "target ↦ value";
- hold, withdraw, supersede and annotate as separate act kinds. Supersede and withdraw are issue acts with another value. Hold, and withdrawal before adoption, are the absence of adoption;
- work outcomes, and any causal "response" relation;
- capability that varies over time;
- drafting time;
- support, frequencies and epistemic-status labels;
- a state/transition view (r0 §2 is withdrawn as unused).

---

## 1. Primitives and definitions

### 1.1 Parameters
**Def 1.1.** Fix the following:
- a finite time set T = {0, 1, …, N}, totally ordered. All three time concepts take values in T; they are different *functions*, not different clocks;
- a finite non-empty set 𝒯 of **targets** (register targets, e.g. the work packages named in A01, A10);
- a finite set V of **deontic values**, and a non-empty subset P ⊆ V of values that **permit work to begin**;
- a finite set Σ of **texts**.

### 1.2 Actors and capability
**Def 1.2.** A history has a finite set 𝒜 of **actors**, and a **capability relation** Cap ⊆ 𝒜 × {iss, adp}. (a, k) ∈ Cap reads "actor a can perform acts of kind k". Capability is constant within a history.

### 1.3 Norm and norm state
**Def 1.3.** A **norm** is a pair (τ, v) ∈ 𝒯 × V. The **norm state** is a function σ : T → V^𝒯. σ(t)(τ) is the value in force for τ at t. σ is a **primitive** of a history. It is not computed from acts, because H-B allows norm changes that are not made by acts (Def 3.1, B-chg).

### 1.4 Acts
**Def 1.4.** A history has a finite set E of norm-making **acts**, partitioned into issue acts E^iss and adoption acts E^adp. Every act a has:
- an actor α(a) ∈ 𝒜;
- a decision time d(a) ∈ T.

Every issue act a ∈ E^iss also has:
- a norm (τ(a), v(a));
- a flag prep(a) ∈ {0, 1}. prep(a) = 1 means "issued as prepared, not adopted";
- an entry into force f(a) ∈ T ∪ {∞}. f(a) = ∞ means the act never enters into force.

Every adoption act b ∈ E^adp has an object obj(b) ∈ E^iss. (This typing is part of the definition. r0 repeated it as a frame axiom F3, which is withdrawn.)

Motivation for using two kinds: the texts separate issuing from adopting (A05: "remains PREPARED, NOT ADOPTED, until the Decision Authority acts on it"; A06; A08 "HELD … NOT ADOPTED"). HYP's status clause needs this split.

### 1.5 Work events
**Def 1.5.** A history has a finite set W of **work events**. Every work event w has:
- a target τ(w);
- an executor α(w) ∈ 𝒜;
- a start time t(w) ∈ T.

### 1.6 Records
**Def 1.6.** A history has a finite set R of **records** (the corpus entries). Every record ρ has:
- a recording time r(ρ) ∈ T;
- a text c(ρ) ∈ Σ;
- a keeper k(ρ) ∈ 𝒜.

It also has two relations:
- a **reference relation** Ref ⊆ R × (E ∪ W). (ρ, x) ∈ Ref reads "ρ carries or references x";
- a partial **constitution map** con : E ⇀ R. con(a) = ρ reads "**ρ is the act a**": making the record is performing the act.

If (ρ, a) ∈ Ref and con(a) ≠ ρ, then ρ **reports** a, and a is a separate act. That act is constituted by another record, or by no record.

### 1.7 History, coordinates, identity
**Def 1.7 (history; coordinates; ≈_X).** A **history** is
h = (𝒜, Cap, E^iss, E^adp, W, R, α, d, τ, v, prep, f, obj, τ_W, α_W, t, r, c, k, Ref, con, σ),
with the components of Defs 1.2–1.6. (τ_W and α_W are the target and executor of work events. Below they are written τ(w) and α(w) where this is unambiguous.) Each component is a **coordinate** of h, compared as follows:
- an item set (𝒜, E^iss, E^adp, W, R) or a relation (Cap, Ref) is compared as a set;
- an attribute (α, d, τ, v, prep, f, obj, τ_W, α_W, t, r, c, k) is compared as a function, *domain included*;
- con is compared as its graph, the set of pairs (a, con(a));
- σ is compared as a function on T.

For a set X of coordinates, **h ≈_X h′** iff h and h′ have the same value on every coordinate outside X. Since an attribute's domain is part of its value, h ≈_X h′ with no item set in X implies that h and h′ have the same items.

**Def 1.7a (cross-history identity).** Fix countably infinite, pairwise disjoint sets of identifiers: 𝔄 (actors), 𝔈 (acts), 𝔚 (work events) and 𝔑 (records). Every history has 𝒜 ⊆ 𝔄, E ⊆ 𝔈, W ⊆ 𝔚 and R ⊆ 𝔑, all finite. The parameters of Def 1.1 are shared by all histories. An actor, act, work event or record of h is **the same** as one of h′ iff it has the same identifier. This is the identity used by ≈_X, by equality of observations (Def 1.11) and by Def 5.1. An identifier is **fresh** for h if it is not among h's items.

**Def 1.7b (replacements and fresh additions).** For a history h:
- h[σ*, f*] is h with σ replaced by σ* and f replaced by f* (on the same E^iss). h[Cap*] is defined in the same way.
- A **fresh addition** to h is a history h⁺ that has the same value as h on every coordinate, except for exactly one of the following changes:
  - **(+actor)** 𝒜⁺ = 𝒜 ∪ {x}, with x fresh. Cap is unchanged;
  - **(+work)** W⁺ = W ∪ {w}, with w fresh and any τ(w) ∈ 𝒯, α(w) ∈ 𝒜, t(w) ∈ T. Ref is unchanged, so w is unreferenced;
  - **(+act)** E^iss⁺ = E^iss ∪ {a}, with a fresh, prep(a) = 1, any norm, any α(a) ∈ 𝒜, any d(a) ∈ T and any f(a) ∈ T ∪ {∞}. Ref and con are unchanged, so a is unreferenced and unconstituted;
  - **(+ref)** Ref⁺ = Ref ∪ {(ρ, x)} for some ρ ∈ R and x ∈ E ∪ W.

  In each case the attributes are extended to the new item and are otherwise unchanged; σ is unchanged.

### 1.8 Structures and frames
**Def 1.8 (structures, frames, base frame 𝓗).** 𝓢 is the set of all histories (Def 1.7). The **base frame** 𝓗 is the set of histories that satisfy these two axioms:
- **F1 (entry into force, Def).** If a ∈ E^iss and f(a) = t ∈ T, then σ(t)(τ(a)) = v(a). This axiom is what "entry into force" means.
- **F2 (the record is the act, Asm).** If con(a) = ρ, then (ρ, a) ∈ Ref and d(a) = r(ρ). This is a modelling assumption: under constitution, the decision time is the recording time. F2 says nothing about entry into force, and it does not assume that any record constitutes any act (con may be undefined everywhere).
- **F3 (typing). WITHDRAWN.** It repeated the typing obj(b) ∈ E^iss already stated in Def 1.4 (M-2).

A **frame** is any subset 𝓗′ ⊆ 𝓗. (r2, B-1: r1 allowed any subset of 𝓢.) Hence **every member of every frame satisfies F1 and F2.** 𝓢, 𝓗 and the frames are relative to the parameters of Def 1.1.

The base frame has no other axiom. In particular it does not require:
- that every act or work event is referenced by some record (H11: non-occurrence may not be read from absence);
- that a norm value implies or excludes any act or work event (H10);
- any order between r, d and f, apart from F2 (H12, H04).

*Check of the r2 restriction (part of Def 1.8).*
- Every frame used in R4 is a subset of 𝓗: 𝓗 itself (the base pair; Lem 4.2, Cor 4.3, §4.5, Lem 5.2 on 𝓗, and CM-A1, CM-A2, CM-A3a, CM-A3b, CM-A4a, CM-A4b, CM-A8); 𝓗₅, 𝓗₇ and 𝓗₉, each of which is 𝓗 plus one further axiom; and the CM-A6 frame, which is 𝓗 for the parameters V = P = {p}. So every countermodel still qualifies, and no countermodel changes.
- The closure hypotheses A5, A7 and A9 (§4.1) remain consistent with the restriction. Let h ∈ 𝓗. Then h[σ*, f*] satisfies F2, because F2 mentions neither σ nor f; every fresh addition to h satisfies F2 (proof of Lem 4.0a, A7); and every change of only con or only d leaves F1 true, because F1 mentions neither. So every history that A5, A7 or A9 puts into 𝓗′ lies in 𝓗.
- The R5 universe U and its variants keep only assignments that satisfy F1 and F2 (§7.1), so they are frames.

### 1.9 The three times
**Def 1.9.** The three times are:
- the **recording time** r(ρ) of a record;
- the **decision time** d(a) of an act;
- the **entry into force** f(a) of an issue act.

The frame equates d and r **only under constitution** (F2: con(a) = ρ ⇒ d(a) = r(ρ)). It never equates f with r or with d. The work start time t(w) is an attribute of work events. It is not one of the three governance times. (G05, H04, A07.)

**Rem 1.9a.** F2 gives no way to read a decision time off a recording time, because con is not observed (Obs O6). Prop 5.4(b) states what would follow if con were observed.

### 1.10 Derived notions
**Def 1.10.** Four derived notions:
- **Adoption.** For a ∈ E^iss and t ∈ T, Adopted(a, t) holds iff either
  - prep(a) = 0, (α(a), adp) ∈ Cap and d(a) ≤ t; or
  - there is b ∈ E^adp with obj(b) = a, (α(b), adp) ∈ Cap and d(b) ≤ t.
- **Entry-into-force data.** F̂(h) = {(a, τ(a), v(a), f(a)) : a ∈ E^iss, f(a) ∈ T}.
- **Change points.** Chg(h) = {(t, τ) : 1 ≤ t ≤ N, σ(t)(τ) ≠ σ(t−1)(τ)}.
- **Violation.** A work event w **violates** in h iff σ(t(w))(τ(w)) ∉ P. Otherwise it **conforms**.

### 1.11 The observation function
**Def 1.11.** The base observation is
> **O(h) = { (ρ, r(ρ), c(ρ)) : ρ ∈ R }**,

the set of record identities with their recording times and texts. More generally, an **observation on a frame 𝓗′** is any function O′ on 𝓗′. O′ **does not depend on** a set X of coordinates **over 𝓗′** iff for all h, h′ ∈ 𝓗′, h ≈_X h′ implies O′(h) = O′(h′). For a class 𝓒 ⊆ 𝓗′ and a value o, the **fibre** is 𝓒 ∩ O′⁻¹(o).

**Rem 1.11a.** The texts c(ρ) are observed **as texts**. A text that says "effective immediately" or "remains blocked" is a value of c, not a value of f or σ. Statements like these are self-assertions (A02, A05, A06). The base frame does not treat them as observations of σ; that is a modelling choice (A5), not a finding that no corpus text states a norm state.

**What O can and cannot see (Obs O1–O9).**

| | Coordinate | Seen by O? | Base |
|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | record identities, recording times r, verbatim texts c | **at most these, and not completely.** Recording times are known as reported, second-hand, and not for every record (A07: "R-80 has no timeline entry"). Verbatim texts exist only where a span exists (F13: R24, R28, R35 have no source span). Capture is local only (G01). The available observation is therefore a function of O that forgets some values. By Lem 1.12 every result below that holds for O also holds for it | A01–A13, A15 (L0, per H01); A07; F13; B06 "RECORDING_ORDER"; G01 |
| O2 | decision time d | **no, not in general** | A07 "Recording times (not decision times)"; F08 "the hour of decision of R-77 and R-79"; G05 |
| O3 | entry into force f (and so F̂) | **no** | G05 "is NOT an upper bound on entry into force"; H12 |
| O4 | norm state σ | **no independent channel.** No locally checkable channel qualifies as an *independent* norm-in-force record (B07, F-B1). Whether one exists anywhere is not determinable (D04). This is not a claim that no corpus text states a norm state; ruling texts do, as self-assertions (Rem 1.11a) | B07; D04; F06; H14 |
| O5 | capability Cap | **no**. Host membership is access, not capability | G07; H19 |
| O6 | constitution con (whether a record *is* the act or *reports* it); reference Ref | **con: not reliably codable on this corpus, within the Claude family, even as a binary distinction** (IF: ACT_SELF_PERFORMED fails for every pair, opus~sonnet 0.598). IF is not an R3 item; IF's pre-registered consequence is "stated, not adopted"; IF shows nothing cross-family. **Ref: no unreliability is shown.** IF reports, exploratorily, that the two capable coders reproduced ACT_REPORTED (1.000) and NORM_STATED (0.941). R4 leaves Ref out of O as a **modelling choice**, and Lem 4.2 shows that 4.1(i) and (ii) do not depend on that choice. B09 (perfect within-family agreement on other fields) supports only the caveat that within-family agreement "is not evidence against correlated error" | IF (not an R3 item); B09 (caveat only); F15 (R2 pending) |
| O7 | keeper k | **no, not in general** | F14; A03 ("no Author line"); F02 |
| O8 | work start time t | **no**. Execution traces give recording order only. File names are not timestamps | B06; G05 (Protocol A L3) |
| O9 | acts and work events that no record references; completeness of the corpus | **no**. Absence is NOT-EVIDENCED-IN-CAPTURE | H11; F08; F11; F13; G01 |

**Lem 1.12.** Over every frame, O does not depend on σ, f, Ref, con, d, Cap, k, or on 𝒜, E, W and their attributes, and O is unchanged by every fresh addition (Def 1.7b). Every function g∘O of O inherits all of these properties. *Proof:* O reads only R, r and c, and none of the listed changes touches them. If O(h) = O(h′), then g(O(h)) = g(O(h′)). ∎

## 3. H-D and H-B as model classes

### 3.1 Clauses (derived only from HYP, except where stated)
**Def 3.1.** These are constraints on h ∈ 𝓢. Each one is followed by the HYP text it formalizes and the reading chosen.

| Clause | Constraint | HYP text; reading |
|---|---|---|
| **D-chg** | for every (t, τ) ∈ Chg(h) there is a ∈ E^iss with τ(a) = τ, f(a) = t, v(a) = σ(t)(τ) and (α(a), iss) ∈ Cap | "norms change **only** through such acts, by actors holding the capability" |
| **D-st** | for every a ∈ E^iss, f(a) < ∞ implies Adopted(a, f(a)) | "the force of a norm depends on the status of the act that made it (e.g. prepared vs adopted)". Read as: force requires adoption. The converse reading (adopted implies in force) is not adopted; see Lem 3.7 |
| (D-wrk) | none | "the governed work itself is outside what the record needs to contain". This allows; it does not constrain |
| **D-rec** | some (ρ, a) ∈ Ref has a ∈ E | "the record is primarily a record of norm-making". Weakest reading. The comparative "primarily" is not formalized, because it would require counting kinds of reference, which is coding-dependent (IF) |
| **B-chg** | for every (t, τ) ∈ Chg(h), **either** there is a ∈ E^iss with τ(a) = τ, f(a) = t and v(a) = σ(t)(τ) (no capability or status condition), **or** some w ∈ W has t(w) < t | "norms change through norm-making acts **and** in response to work". "In response to" is formalized only as temporal precedence, **on any target** (Rem 3.1b). A response relation would be a new primitive that the base does not need |
| **B-conf** | every w ∈ W conforms | "work is expected to conform … (execution begins only when permitted)". **Universal reading, a modelling choice taken from E01 (L1), not from HYP** (Rem 3.1a) |
| (B-fb) | no constraint beyond B-chg's second disjunct | "work outcomes feed back into norm changes". Allowed, not required. The model has no outcome attribute |
| **B-recW** | some (ρ, w) ∈ Ref has w ∈ W | together with D-rec: "the record is expected to carry, or reference, both" |
| **B-rec** | D-rec ∧ B-recW | |

**Rem 3.1a (B-conf's universal reading is a modelling choice).** HYP says only that work "is expected to conform". The universal reading "every work event conforms" is taken from E01 (L1 data: "refutes only a universal 'all recorded work conforms'"), not from HYP. It makes H-B refutable by a single violating work event, while H-D has no work clause of comparable strength. This asymmetry is a consequence of the chosen reading, not a finding about the hypotheses. A weaker (non-universal) reading is not modelled.

**Rem 3.1b (B-chg's any-target vacuity).** B-chg's work disjunct accepts work on **any** target at **any** earlier time. So once any work event precedes t, B-chg holds at t for every target, and B-chg is nearly vacuous after the first work event. This is a disclosed modelling choice (the weakest reading of "in response to"). A target-tied variant (τ(w) = τ) is not adopted.

**Rem 3.1c (unformalized clauses).** B-fb and the comparative "primarily" are not formalized. The first omission weakens H-B and the second weakens D-rec. Both are roughly symmetric, and neither class is built into the primitives, the frame or O.

**Def 3.2.** The model classes are:
- **H-D** = {h ∈ 𝓗 : D-chg ∧ D-st ∧ D-rec};
- **H-B** = {h ∈ 𝓗 : B-chg ∧ B-conf ∧ B-rec};
- **R_B** = {h ∈ 𝓗 : B-rec}.

For a frame 𝓗′, the primed classes **H-D′**, **H-B′** and **R_B′** are defined by the same clauses with 𝓗′ in place of 𝓗. These are sets of histories. Nothing in R4 asserts that the actual history lies in either set (H07).

### 3.2 The exact relation
**Lem 3.3.** D-chg ⇒ B-chg, and B-rec ⇒ D-rec. Neither converse holds. *Proof:* The witness for D-chg is a witness for B-chg's first disjunct, and B-rec contains D-rec. For the converses, see Lem 3.5(b) and (a′). ∎

**Prop 3.4 (near nesting).**
> H-D ∩ H-B = H-D ∩ B-conf ∩ B-recW = H-B ∩ D-chg ∩ D-st.

Hence:
- H-D ∖ H-B = H-D ∖ (B-conf ∩ B-recW);
- H-B ∖ H-D = H-B ∖ (D-chg ∩ D-st).

Each class is contained in the other once exactly two of the other's clauses are added:
- H-D ∩ B-conf ∩ B-recW ⊆ H-B;
- H-B ∩ D-chg ∩ D-st ⊆ H-D.

*Proof:* If h ∈ H-D satisfies B-conf and B-recW, then B-chg holds by Lem 3.3, and B-rec = D-rec ∧ B-recW. So h ∈ H-B. If h ∈ H-B satisfies D-chg and D-st, then D-rec holds by Lem 3.3. D-wrk adds nothing. So h ∈ H-D. The reverse inclusions hold because H-D ∩ H-B satisfies all the clauses. ∎

**Lem 3.5 (neither class contains the other).** Take T = {0, 1}, 𝒯 = {τ}, V = {p, q}, P = {p} and 𝒜 = {x}. The record ρ has some fixed r(ρ) and c(ρ), the same in every item below.
- **(a) A history in H-D ∖ H-B.** E = {a} with a an issue act: (τ, q), prep 1, f = ∞. W = {w} with t(w) = 0. R = {ρ} with Ref = {(ρ, a), (ρ, w)}. σ ≡ q. Then h ∈ H-D, and w violates.
- **(a′) Another history in H-D ∖ H-B.** The same, but with W = ∅ and Ref = {(ρ, a)}. Then h ∈ H-D, and B-recW fails.
- **(b) A history in H-B ∖ H-D.** As in (a), but σ(0) = p, σ(1) = q and t(w) = 0. The change at 1 is explained by earlier work, so B-chg holds. B-conf and B-rec hold. D-chg fails, because no act enters into force at 1.
- **(b′) WITHDRAWN.** In (b′) B-chg also holds through the work disjunct, so it added nothing beyond (b) (M-6).

∎

**Lem 3.6 (shared acceptance of acts; G06).** H-D ∪ H-B ⊆ {h : E ≠ ∅}. *Proof:* Both classes require D-rec. ∎

**Lem 3.7 (the biconditional status reading).** Let D-st⁺ be D-st together with "if Adopted(a, t) holds for some t, then f(a) < ∞". Let H-D⁺′ be H-D′ with D-st⁺ in place of D-st. Let (O′, 𝓗′) satisfy A1, A2 and A5 (§4.1), and the side conditions:
- **(SC1)** 𝓗′ is closed under h ↦ h[Cap := ∅];
- **(SC2)** O′ does not depend on Cap over 𝓗′.

Then Prop 4.1(i) holds with H-D⁺′ in place of H-D′. The base pair (O, 𝓗) satisfies SC1, because no axiom of 𝓗 mentions Cap, and SC2 by Lem 1.12.

*Proof:* Take h* from the proof of 4.1(i). Let h** = h*[Cap := ∅]. Then h** ∈ 𝓗′ by SC1, and O′(h**) = O′(h*) = O′(h) by SC2. No act is adopted in h**, because Adopted requires capability, so the extra clause of D-st⁺ is vacuous. f** ≡ ∞, so D-st is vacuous. D-chg is vacuous, because σ** is constant. D-rec is unchanged, and the H-B clauses do not mention Cap. ∎

## 4. D1 as a proposition

### 4.1 Hypotheses
A1–A9 are **hypotheses (Hyp) of the generic results** about a pair (O′, 𝓗′), where 𝓗′ is a frame and O′ an observation on 𝓗′. Lem 4.0a shows that the base pair (O, 𝓗) satisfies all of them except A6, which is a parameter condition. They are **pairwise independent**: §4.4 gives, for each one, a countermodel that violates it and satisfies all the others.

| | Hypothesis | Kind | Motivation (base) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A1** | O′ does not depend on σ over 𝓗′ | observation | O4: B07, D04, F06 |
| **A2** | O′ does not depend on f over 𝓗′ | observation | O3: G05, H12 |
| **A3** | O′ does not depend on Ref or con over 𝓗′ | observation | O6 (con: IF, within-family; Ref: modelling choice) |
| **A4** | **Invariance under fresh additions.** O′(h⁺) = O′(h) whenever h, h⁺ ∈ 𝓗′ and h⁺ is a fresh addition to h of kind (+actor), (+work) or (+act) (Def 1.7b). A4 says nothing about f, d, Ref or con of existing items | observation | O7, O8, O9 |
| **A5** | **Neutrality for σ and f.** For every h ∈ 𝓗′ and all σ*, f*: if h[σ*, f*] satisfies F1, then h[σ*, f*] ∈ 𝓗′. In other words, 𝓗′ constrains σ and f only through F1, and no frame axiom ties any other coordinate to σ or f | frame | O4: B07 (no local channel is an *independent* norm-in-force record); D04. This is a modelling choice. It is not a claim that no attestation exists anywhere (H14), or that no corpus text states a norm state (Rem 1.11a) |
| **A6** | P ≠ V | parameter | otherwise no work can violate |
| **A7** | **Openness.** For every h ∈ 𝓗′, every fresh addition h⁺ to h of any of the four kinds that satisfies F1 is in 𝓗′. The frame thus admits actors, work events and prepared issue acts that no record references, and it does not constrain which items records reference | frame | H11; F08; F11; O9 |
| **A8** | O′ does not depend on d over 𝓗′ | observation | O2: A07, F08 |
| **A9** | **No c–con tie (neutrality for con and d).** For every h ∈ 𝓗′, every history obtained from h by changing only con, or only d, that satisfies F2 is in 𝓗′. In particular no frame axiom ties the text c (or any other coordinate) to con | frame | O6; IF's candidate concept (Conj 5.5) |

Where the hypotheses are used:
- Prop 4.1(i): A1, A2, A5;
- 4.1(i′): A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A7;
- 4.1(ii): A1, A2, A5, A6;
- 4.1(iii): A1, A2, A4, A5, A7;
- Lem 5.2: A3, A8, A9, and also A1, A2, A5 for its H-D cases.

**Lem 4.0a (the base pair satisfies the hypotheses).** (O, 𝓗) satisfies A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A7, A8 and A9. A6 is a condition on the parameters only.

*Proof:*
- A1, A2, A3, A4 and A8 follow from Lem 1.12.
- A5: F2 mentions neither σ nor f, so h[σ*, f*] satisfies F2 whenever h does, and F1 is assumed.
- A7: a fresh actor or work event does not touch F1 or F2. A fresh (+act) item is unconstituted, so F2 holds for it, and F1 is assumed. A (+ref) addition cannot break F2, since F2 only requires certain pairs to be in Ref.
- A9: F1 mentions neither con nor d, and F2 is assumed. ∎

**Lem 4.0b (joint non-dependence on σ and f).** Assume A1, A2 and A5. Let h ∈ 𝓗′, and let σ*, f* be such that h[σ*, f*] satisfies F1. Then h[σ*, f*] ∈ 𝓗′ and O′(h[σ*, f*]) = O′(h).

*Proof:* Let f^∞ ≡ ∞ on E^iss. Define the intermediate histories
- h¹ = h[σ, f^∞];
- h² = h[σ*, f^∞];
- h³ = h[σ*, f*].

h¹ and h² satisfy F1 vacuously, and h³ satisfies it by assumption. Each is h[·, ·] for an F1-satisfying replacement, so all three are in 𝓗′ by A5. Now:
- h ≈_{f} h¹, so O′(h¹) = O′(h) by A2;
- h¹ ≈_{σ} h², so O′(h²) = O′(h¹) by A1;
- h² ≈_{f} h³, so O′(h³) = O′(h²) by A2. ∎

Separate non-dependence on σ and on f thus gives joint non-dependence, through histories that stay in the frame.

### 4.2 Statement
**Prop 4.1 (D1; generic).** Let 𝓗′ be a frame and O′ an observation on 𝓗′.
- **(i) Core.** Assume A1, A2 and A5. For every h ∈ R_B′ there is h* ∈ H-D′ ∩ H-B′ with h* ≈_{σ, f} h and O′(h*) = O′(h). Hence
  > O′(H-D′ ∩ R_B′) = O′(H-B′) = O′(H-D′ ∩ H-B′) = O′(R_B′).
- **(i′) Record clauses.** Assume A1, A2, A3, A4, A5 and A7. Then
  > O′(H-D′) = O′(H-B′) = O′(H-D′ ∩ H-B′) = {O′(h) : h ∈ 𝓗′, R_h ≠ ∅}.
- **(ii) The contrast.** Assume A1, A2, A5 and A6. Let h ∈ R_B′, and let w be a work event referenced in h. There are h_v and h_c, both ≈_{σ, f} h, with **O′(h_v) = O′(h_c) = O′(h)**, such that:
  - h_v ∈ H-D′ ∖ H-B′, σ_v is constant on T, and w **violates a norm that never changes**;
  - h_c ∈ H-D′ ∩ H-B′, and every work event conforms.
- **(iii) H5's wording, local form.** Assume A1, A2, A4, A5 and A7. Let h ∈ H-D′ ∩ R_B′, and let w violate in h. Then there is h′ ∈ H-B′ with O′(h′) = O′(h) such that:
  - h′ differs from h only in σ (and only at violation points of h), in f, and by additional prepared issue acts that no record references and no record constitutes;
  - w conforms in h′;
  - every change point of σ′ at which no act of h enters into force (in h′) with the new value is the entry into force of an added act.

**Cor 4.1b (the base case).** For (O, 𝓗):
- (i), (i′) and (iii) hold;
- (ii) holds whenever P ≠ V;
- in (i′), {O(h) : h ∈ 𝓗, R_h ≠ ∅} = {o ∈ O(𝓗) : o ≠ ∅}.

*Proof:* Lem 4.0a and Prop 4.1. O(h) = ∅ iff R_h = ∅. ∎

**Rem 4.1a (in words).** On any observation satisfying the hypotheses, "the work violated an unchanged norm" and "the norm state at t(w) was different" are not separated ((ii), (iii)). (iii) adds that the difference can be carried by acts that no record references, which is H5's "without a recorded act". **Only this last clause needs A7.** In a frame where every item must be referenced, the non-separation itself survives, through added acts that are referenced (CM-A7(b)).

**Lem 4.2 (robustness).** Prop 4.1(i) holds for every (O′, 𝓗′) satisfying A1, A2 and A5, and (ii) holds if A6 holds as well; neither needs A3, A4, A7 or A8. In particular, on 𝓗 they hold for O_¬σf, the observation of **every coordinate except σ and f**. O_¬σf sees Ref, con, d, Cap, k, 𝒜, E, W and all their attributes **other than f**. So (i) and (ii) hold even if the reference and mode coding were perfectly reliable. *Proof:* The first sentence is the hypothesis list of Prop 4.1(i) and (ii). O_¬σf satisfies A1 and A2 on 𝓗, because h ≈_σ h′ or h ≈_f h′ leaves every other coordinate unchanged, and 𝓗 satisfies A5 (Lem 4.0a). ∎

**Cor 4.3 (separation requires dependence on σ or f).** Assume A5 for 𝓗′. If O′(H-D′ ∩ R_B′) ≠ O′(H-B′), then O′ depends, over 𝓗′, on σ or on f. In particular, on 𝓗, no observation that is a function of coordinates other than σ and f separates the classes on R_B. This includes any function of the records, their keepers, Ref, con, Cap, and the acts and work events with their attributes **other than f**. *Proof:* This is the contrapositive of Lem 4.2. ∎

Cor 4.3 derives **only** that a separating observation must depend on σ or f. It does **not** derive the further elements of H5 §5.2's necessary condition: independence from the norm-maker, the executor and the self-asserting ruling, and the mapping to a target at t. Those appear only in the sufficient conditions (§4.5) and in Def 4.9. O₂ in CM-A2 depends on f and does separate, as Cor 4.3 allows.

### 4.3 Proofs
***Proof of (i).*** Fix p ∈ P. By Lem 4.0b, with σ* ≡ p and f* ≡ ∞ (so F1 holds vacuously), h* := h[σ*, f*] ∈ 𝓗′ and O′(h*) = O′(h). Then:
- *H-D′:* Chg(h*) = ∅, so D-chg holds. No act enters into force, so D-st holds. D-rec is inherited from h ∈ R_B′, since Ref is unchanged.
- *H-B′:* B-chg holds vacuously. σ* ≡ p gives B-conf. B-rec is inherited.

For the equalities: H-D′ ∩ H-B′ ⊆ H-D′ ∩ R_B′ ⊆ R_B′, and H-D′ ∩ H-B′ ⊆ H-B′ ⊆ R_B′. By the construction, O′(R_B′) ⊆ O′(H-D′ ∩ H-B′). ∎

***Proof of (i′)*** (r2: re-proved; frames are subsets of 𝓗, Def 1.8). Write S := {O′(h) : h ∈ 𝓗′, R_h ≠ ∅}.

*S ⊆ O′(H-D′ ∩ H-B′).* Let h ∈ 𝓗′ with R ≠ ∅. Since 𝓗′ ⊆ 𝓗, h satisfies F1. Pick ρ₀ ∈ R, τ₀ ∈ 𝒯 and v₀ ∈ V. Apply these fresh additions in turn:
1. if 𝒜 = ∅, (+actor) with a fresh x; otherwise let x ∈ 𝒜;
2. (+act) a fresh a₀ with norm (τ₀, v₀), prep 1, α(a₀) = x, d(a₀) = 0 and f(a₀) = ∞ (x ∈ 𝒜 after step 1);
3. (+work) a fresh w₀ with τ(w₀) = τ₀, α(w₀) = x and t(w₀) = 0;
4. (+ref) (ρ₀, a₀);
5. (+ref) (ρ₀, w₀).

Each intermediate history satisfies F1. The history before step 1 is h, which satisfies F1. Steps 1, 3, 4 and 5 change none of E^iss, τ, v, f and σ, which are the only coordinates F1 reads, so they preserve F1. Step 2 leaves σ and every existing act unchanged, and adds a₀ with f(a₀) = ∞, which imposes no F1 condition; so it preserves F1 too. Each step is a fresh addition (Def 1.7b) to a history that is already in 𝓗′ (for step 1, h; afterwards, by the previous step), and its result satisfies F1. So each result is in 𝓗′ by A7. Steps 1–3 are fresh additions of kinds (+actor), (+act) and (+work), so they leave O′ unchanged by A4. Steps 4 and 5 change only Ref, so they leave O′ unchanged by A3. Let h̃ be the result. Then h̃ ∈ 𝓗′ and O′(h̃) = O′(h). h̃ satisfies D-rec through (ρ₀, a₀) ∈ Ref with a₀ ∈ E, and B-recW through (ρ₀, w₀) ∈ Ref with w₀ ∈ W, so h̃ ∈ R_B′. By (i), which needs A1, A2 and A5, there is h̃* ∈ H-D′ ∩ H-B′ with O′(h̃*) = O′(h̃) = O′(h).

*O′(H-D′) ⊆ S and O′(H-B′) ⊆ S.* Every h in H-D′ or in H-B′ satisfies D-rec (H-B′ through B-rec), which needs a pair (ρ, a) ∈ Ref with ρ ∈ R. So R_h ≠ ∅.

*The equalities.* O′(H-D′ ∩ H-B′) is contained in O′(H-D′) and in O′(H-B′), both of which are contained in S, which is contained in O′(H-D′ ∩ H-B′). So all four sets are equal. ∎

***Proof of (ii).*** Take h_c = h* from (i). For h_v, choose q ∈ V ∖ P (A6), and let h_v = h[σ ≡ q, f ≡ ∞]. By Lem 4.0b, h_v ∈ 𝓗′ and O′(h_v) = O′(h). h_v ∈ H-D′ as in (i). The work event w exists by R_B′ and violates, so h_v ∉ H-B′. σ_v has no change points. ∎

***Proof of (iii)*** (r2: re-proved; frames are subsets of 𝓗, Def 1.8). Fix p ∈ P (P ≠ ∅ by Def 1.1). Since h ∈ 𝓗′ ⊆ 𝓗, h satisfies F1. Let Vio = {(t(w), τ(w)) : w violates in h}.
- **Step 1 (σ and f).** Let σ′ = σ, except that σ′(t)(τ) = p for (t, τ) ∈ Vio. Let f′(a) = ∞ if f(a) ∈ T and (f(a), τ(a)) ∈ Vio, and f′(a) = f(a) otherwise. *h[σ′, f′] satisfies F1:* let a ∈ E^iss with f′(a) = t ∈ T. Then f(a) = t and (t, τ(a)) ∉ Vio, so σ′(t)(τ(a)) = σ(t)(τ(a)), and σ(t)(τ(a)) = v(a) by F1 in h. By Lem 4.0b (A1, A2, A5), h² := h[σ′, f′] ∈ 𝓗′ and O′(h²) = O′(h). (By F1 in h, an act a with f(a) ∈ T and f′(a) = ∞ has v(a) = σ(f(a))(τ(a)), and this value is not in P, because a work event violates at (f(a), τ(a)). These are exactly the acts in force at a violation point.)
- **Step 2 (added acts).** Let L be the set of (t, τ) ∈ Chg(h²) for which there is no a ∈ E^iss with τ(a) = τ, f′(a) = t and v(a) = σ′(t)(τ). 𝒜 ≠ ∅, because h ∈ R_B′ satisfies B-recW, so some work event exists and its executor is in 𝒜; fix x ∈ 𝒜. For each (t, τ) ∈ L in turn, apply (+act) with a fresh act a_{t,τ} of norm (τ, σ′(t)(τ)), prep 1, α = x and d = f = t. The history before each addition satisfies F1 (h² does, and by induction). The addition changes neither σ′ nor any existing act, and the new act's own F1 condition is σ′(t)(τ) = v(a_{t,τ}), which holds by the choice of v. So each result satisfies F1. It is a fresh addition to a history in 𝓗′, so it is in 𝓗′ by A7, and O′ is unchanged by A4. Let h′ be the final history. Then h′ ∈ 𝓗′ and O′(h′) = O′(h²) = O′(h).

Check that h′ ∈ H-B′:
- *B-chg:* σ_{h′} = σ′, so Chg(h′) = Chg(h²). Let (t, τ) ∈ Chg(h′). If (t, τ) ∉ L, some original act a has τ(a) = τ, f′(a) = t and v(a) = σ′(t)(τ). If (t, τ) ∈ L, the added act a_{t,τ} has these properties. Either way B-chg's act disjunct holds.
- *B-conf:* W_{h′} = W_h. Let w′ ∈ W. If (t(w′), τ(w′)) ∈ Vio, then σ′ has the value p ∈ P there. Otherwise w′ does not violate in h (if it did, its point would be in Vio), so σ(t(w′))(τ(w′)) ∈ P, and σ′ = σ at that point. So w′ conforms in h′.
- *B-rec:* Ref_{h′} = Ref_h, and E and W only grow. So the D-rec pair and the B-recW pair of h are pairs of h′.

The three bullets of (iii):
- h′ differs from h only in σ (σ′ ≠ σ only on Vio, the violation points of h), in f (f′, extended to the added acts), and by the added acts a_{t,τ}. These are prepared (prep 1). Ref and con are unchanged, so no record references or constitutes them.
- w violates in h, so (t(w), τ(w)) ∈ Vio, and w conforms in h′.
- A change point of σ′ at which no act of h enters into force under f′ with the new value is, by definition, a member of L. Each (t, τ) ∈ L is the entry into force f(a_{t,τ}) = t of the added act a_{t,τ} on τ. ∎

### 4.5 Sufficient conditions on an additional observable
**Def 4.4.** An additional observable is a function Q on 𝓗. The joint observation is O_Q = (O, Q). H-D and H-B are **distinguishable under O_Q** iff O_Q(H-D) ≠ O_Q(H-B). An outcome y **excludes H-B** iff y ∈ O_Q(H-D) ∖ O_Q(H-B). An outcome **excludes H-D** iff it lies in O_Q(H-B) ∖ O_Q(H-D).

**Prop 4.5 (sufficient for an outcome that excludes H-B).** Let Q(h) be a set of pairs (λ, v) with labels λ from a fixed set Λ.
- **S1 (veridical and mapped at h).** This is a property of Q at a single history h: there is a partial map μ_h : Λ → W_h such that, for every (λ, v) ∈ Q(h), μ_h(λ) is defined and v = σ_h(t(μ_h(λ)))(τ(μ_h(λ))). So at h, Q reports the norm state **for the target of a work event, at that event's start time**.
- **S2 (realizable).** Some h ∈ H-D has some (λ, v) ∈ Q(h) with v ∉ P.
- **S3 (veridical on H-B).** S1 holds at **every h ∈ H-B**. Nothing is required on 𝓗 ∖ H-B, and in particular nothing on H-D ∖ H-B. (r0 called S3 "non-circular" and required S1 on all of 𝓗; that requirement is withdrawn as unnecessary, see Lem 4.8.)

If S2 and S3 hold, then the outcome O_Q(h) of the S2 witness h excludes H-B, so the classes are distinguishable.

*Proof:* O_Q(h) ∈ O_Q(H-D), because h ∈ H-D. Suppose h′ ∈ H-B had O_Q(h′) = O_Q(h). Then (λ, v) ∈ Q(h′). By S3, S1 holds at h′, so μ_{h′}(λ) is a work event of h′ at which σ_{h′} has the value v ∉ P. That work event violates, which contradicts B-conf. ∎

**Rem 4.5 (r0's unlabelled remark after Prop 4.5). WITHDRAWN.** r0 said: "Such a Q only ever excludes H-B. It never excludes H-D, because the trivial construction of 4.1(i) keeps any Q-value equal to p. This matches E01's direction." *Reason:* the claim is false (Ex 4.5a), and its justification was invalid. A Q-veridicality axiom on the frame mentions σ, so A5 fails and 4.1(i) does not apply. Also, if |P| ≥ 2, setting σ ≡ p changes reported values in P ∖ {p}. No R4 statement now links Prop 4.5 to E01's "H-D makes no prediction".

**Ex 4.5a (Q*: a Q satisfying S1–S3 with an outcome that excludes H-D).** Take the parameters of Lem 3.5, and fix a work identifier w₁ ∈ 𝔚. Let Λ = {λ₁, λ₂}. If w₁ ∈ W_h, let μ_h(λ₁) = μ_h(λ₂) = w₁. If w₁ ∉ W_h, μ_h is the empty partial map (r2, NB-1). Let
- Q*(h) = ∅ if w₁ ∉ W_h;
- otherwise Q*(h) = {(λ₁, s_h)} ∪ {(λ₂, s_h) : h ∉ H-D}, where s_h = σ_h(t(w₁))(τ(w₁)).

Then:
- **(a)** S1 holds at every h ∈ 𝓗, by construction (vacuously when w₁ ∉ W_h, since Q*(h) = ∅ there), so S3 holds;
- **(b)** S2 holds: h_a = Lem 3.5(a) with w = w₁ is in H-D, and Q*(h_a) = {(λ₁, q)} with q ∉ P. By Prop 4.5, O_{Q*}(h_a) excludes H-B;
- **(c)** h_b = Lem 3.5(b) with w = w₁ is in H-B ∖ H-D, and Q*(h_b) = {(λ₁, p), (λ₂, p)}, since σ(0) = p and t(w₁) = 0. Every h′ whose Q*-value contains a λ₂-pair is outside H-D. So O_{Q*}(h_b) ∈ O_{Q*}(H-B) ∖ O_{Q*}(H-D): **this outcome excludes H-D.** ∎

Q* reads class membership. It is a formal counterexample to the withdrawn remark, not a proposed instrument.

Lem V3.9(d): H-D ∩ H-B^g⁺ ⊆ H-D ∩ H-B^g, so its members have the Cap property; the witness h_b must be changed so that an act enters at N: give a the norm (τ, q), prep 1 and f = N (F1 holds, σ(N)(τ) = q). Then a explains the change at N without capability, w precedes it, Cap = ∅, and h_b ∈ H-B^g⁺. Lem V3.10(a): its history has a entering at N with value σ(N)(τ), so it satisfies the act conjunct. Lem V3.10(b): Lem V2.6(ii-v) needs only M_q^D and N_q. ∎

341	### 3.12 R-k (r1, review M3: status- or capability-tied act disjunct)
342	**Lem V3.18.** Both variants R-k^st and R-k^cap have M, M_q^D and N_q, but not T. On 𝓗 (T = {0, 1}), R4's I₇ is in H-D ∩ R_B, its work event violates, and no h′ as in Prop 4.1(iii) is in H-B^k.

344	*Proof.* Record clauses and B-conf are 𝐑₀'s. B-chg^k constrains only change points, so it holds on every quiescent history: M_p, M_q^D. N_q through B-conf. *Where T breaks:* I₇ as in Lem V3.12(b): σ′ = (q, p) is forced, with a change at 1; there is no work before 1; a has v = q. R4's added acts are issue acts with prep 1 and no adoption act (fresh additions add no adoption acts), so they are not adopted (R-k^st fails); Cap is unchanged and Cap = ∅ in I₇, so they are not iss-capable (R-k^cap fails). ∎

Both qualifiers occur only in the H-D list. Reading them into B-chg imports H-D's clauses (D-chg's capability, D-st's status) into H-B, so the reading is not derived from H-B's text, and it narrows the very contrast HYP states. 350	## 4. Combinations
351	
352	**Lem V4.1 (r1: relabelled from Rem; interacting combinations).** Readings that replace the **same** clause are not combined.
353	- **(a)** Among the M-readings R-a, R-b, R-e, R-f, R-h and R-k, every pair that replaces distinct clauses has M, **except R-c = R-b ∘ R-f**, which is not-M (Lem V3.3).
354	- **(b) R-g ∘ R-f** is not-M. Its S-form counterexamples include every S-form counterexample of R-g and every member of the D-rec class with W = ∅.
355	- **(c) R-d ∘ R-e.** For the image equalities of (i) under SC1 and SC2 there is no interaction: Lem 3.7's h** has Chg = ∅, and D-chg^e is vacuous there. **The S-form failure set does interact:** the S-form counterexamples of R-d ∘ R-e are S-form counterexamples of R-d, but not conversely; h₁ of Lem V3.6(b) is not a counterexample under R-d ∘ R-e.
356	- **(d) R-d ∘ R-c.** For the base pair the image equalities of (i) hold. The S-form fails; its counterexamples include R-c's (members of D-rec with W = ∅) and h₁ of Lem V3.6(b).
357	- **(e) R-a ∘ R-g** (target-tied work-responsive change) needs two targets. **UNTESTABLE IN U.**
358	
359	*Proof.* (a) The record base of a pair is that of whichever member changes B-rec: R_B, R_B^f = D-rec or R_B^h. RB1 and RB2 hold for each (Lem V2.5, V3.8, V3.11). D-chg^e, B-chg^a, B-chg^k, D-chg, D-st and B-chg are vacuous on quiescent histories (Chg = ∅, f ≡ ∞). Universal B-conf holds on every p-quiescent history. B-conf^b holds on a p-quiescent history iff W ≠ ∅; this is guaranteed on R_B and R_B^h (B-recW) and not on R_B^f (Lem V3.3(a)). So M_p fails only for R-b ∘ R-f.
360	(b) A member of D-rec with W = ∅: every h′ ≈_{σ, f} has W = ∅ and fails B-chg^g. An R-g counterexample h ∈ R_B: any h′ ≈_{σ, f} h has h's Ref, E and W, so satisfies B-rec, and h′ ∈ H-B^{g∘f} iff h′ ∈ H-B^g. Not-M follows from Lem V3.9(a), whose witness lies in R_B ⊆ D-rec.
361	(c) H-D^{d∘e} ⊇ H-D⁺ (D-chg ⇒ D-chg^e), so an R-d ∘ R-e counterexample is an R-d counterexample. For h₁: take f*(a) = 1 and σ* = (p, q). F1 holds; the change at 1 is explained by a without capability (D-chg^e); a is adopted at 1 (D-st, D-st⁺); w at 0 conforms; B-chg holds through a; Ref is unchanged. So h₁ has h* ∈ H-D^{d∘e} ∩ H-B.
362	(d) *Images:* let h ∈ D-rec. If W = ∅, apply (+work) with a fresh unreferenced w₀ (A7; O unchanged, Lem 1.12). Then Cap := ∅ (SC1, SC2 hold for the base pair, R4 Lem 3.7), then σ ≡ p, f ≡ ∞ (Lem 4.0b). The result satisfies D-chg (Chg = ∅), D-st (f ≡ ∞), D-st⁺ (nothing adopted), D-rec (Ref unchanged), B-chg (vacuous), B-conf^b (W ≠ ∅, all conform) and B-rec^c = D-rec, and has observation O(h). The reverse inclusions are as in Lem V2.6(i). *S-form:* an R-c counterexample h has W = ∅ throughout its ≈_{σ, f}-class, so B-conf^b fails there. For h₁, the case analysis of Lem V3.6(b) applies unchanged, because h₁ has a single work event, so B-conf^b and B-conf agree on its class. ∎

- (d) Prop 4.1(i) also fails for R-i under A1, A2, A5 at a nonempty observation: (O₃, 𝓗) with O₃ = (O, Ref) (CM-A3a) satisfies A1, A2, A5 and has O₃(H-B^i) ⊄ O₃(H-D ∩ R_B^i). The same holds for R-i′.

*Proof.* (a) RB1: E ≠ ∅ reads only E; the empty clause set reads nothing. M_p, M_q^D, N_q and T1: the dyn clauses are 𝐑₀'s, and Lem V2.5's checks of them do not use the record clause. T2: E ≠ ∅ is preserved by (+act). *Where the construction breaks (RB2):* let h ∈ 𝓗 have E = {a} (an issue act, prep 1, f = ∞) and Ref = ∅. Then h ∈ R_B^i ⊆ R_B^{i′}, but h fails D-rec, so 𝔅_rec does not imply 𝔇_rec.
(b) The same h. Every h* ≈_{σ, f} h has Ref = ∅, so it fails D-rec and h* ∉ H-D^𝐑.
(c) H-D ⊆ D-rec ⊆ {E ≠ ∅} (Lem 3.6), so H-D ∩ R_B^𝐑 = H-D, and O(H-D) = {o ≠ ∅} (R4 Cor 4.1b, (i′): D-rec needs a record). H-D ∩ H-B ⊆ H-D ∩ H-B^𝐑 ⊆ H-D, since B-rec ⇒ D-rec ⇒ E ≠ ∅; R4 Cor 4.1b gives O(H-D ∩ H-B) = {o ≠ ∅}, so O(H-D ∩ H-B^𝐑) = {o ≠ ∅}. Let h₀ have E = {a} (prep 1, f = ∞), W = ∅, R = ∅, Ref = ∅, σ ≡ p. Then h₀ ∈ 𝓗, B-chg and B-conf hold vacuously and E ≠ ∅, so h₀ ∈ H-B^i ⊆ H-B^{i′}, and O(h₀) = ∅. So O(H-B^𝐑) ⊇ {o ≠ ∅} ∪ {∅} = O(𝓗), and O(R_B^𝐑) ⊆ O(𝓗). ∅ ∈ O(H-B^𝐑) ∖ O(H-D ∩ R_B^𝐑).
(d) O₃ satisfies A1 and A2 on 𝓗 (Ref is unchanged by σ, f), and 𝓗 satisfies A5. Let h have R = {ρ}, E = {a} (prep 1, f = ∞), W = ∅, Ref = ∅, σ ≡ p. Then h ∈ H-B^i, and every h′ with O₃(h′) = O₃(h) has Ref = ∅, so fails D-rec. So O₃(h) ∈ O₃(H-B^i) ∖ O₃(H-D ∩ R_B^i). ∎

**Lem V3.14 (R-i, R-i′: what survives).**
- (a) For the base pair, the image equalities of (i) hold on nonempty observations: for every o ≠ ∅, o lies in all four images.
- (b) (ii): the S-form fails on 𝓗 (both halves, at any h ∈ R_B^𝐑 with a referenced w and no referenced act). Under A1, A2, **A3**, A5, A6, **A7**, Prop 4.1(ii) holds in its O-form ("same O′" instead of ≈_{σ, f}).
- (c) Prop 4.1(iii) holds for R-i and R-i′ with R4's proof (Lem V2.6(iii); T holds), with starting class H-D ∩ R_B^𝐑 = H-D.

*Proof.* (a) Lem V3.13(c). (b) *S-form:* h_v and h_c must be in H-D^𝐑, which needs D-rec, and Ref is fixed under ≈_{σ, f}. *O-form:* h ∈ R_B^𝐑 with w referenced has some ρ ∈ R; if Ref has no act pair, h has an act (R-i) or, for R-i′, first apply (+act) (A7; O′ unchanged by A4 — so for R-i′ also assume **A4**); then apply (+ref) (ρ, a) for an act a (A7; O′ unchanged by A3). The result h̃ is in R_B with w referenced, and R4's (ii) applied to h̃ gives h_v, h_c with O′ = O′(h). (c) Lem V2.6(iii) and Lem 3.6. ∎

**Rem V3.14a (revision flag; testability).** If R-i or R-i′ were adopted, **R4 would have to be revised**: Prop 4.1(i), (i′) and the S-form of (ii) fail as stated; Cor 4.1b fails at o = ∅; Lem 4.2 fails (O_¬σf sees Ref, and Lem V3.13(b)'s h separates under it); Cor 4.3 fails. The base-pair failure at o = ∅ is **UNTESTABLE IN U**, because ρ1 is always present. The S-form failures and the O₃ separation are testable in U (`V1B-PREDICTIONS.md`). Nothing is revised here.

### 3.10 R-j (r1, review M2: D-side descriptive change)
**Lem V3.15 (R-j is not-M).**
- (a) R-j satisfies RB1, RB2, N_q and T, but neither M_p^W nor M_q^D.
- (b) The S-form of (i) fails on 𝓗, and Prop 4.1(i) fails for (O_¬σf, 𝓗) (N ≥ 1, parameters of R4 Lem 3.5).
- (c) At N = 0, **H-D^j = ∅: the reading is inconsistent**, as R-g is (Lem V3.9(b)).
- (d) The h_v half of Prop 4.1(ii) fails **for every pair**: H-D^j contains no history with constant σ.

*Proof.* (a) Record clauses and the B side are 𝐑₀'s (RB1, RB2, N_q, T). *Where the construction breaks:* every quiescent g has Chg(g) = ∅, so D-chg^j fails at every quiescent history (M_p^W and M_q^D fail).
(b) Let h ∈ R_B have Cap = ∅ (e.g. R4 Lem 3.5(a) with σ ≡ p). Every h′ ≈_{σ, f} h has Cap = ∅. D-chg^j needs a change point with an iss-capable act, so h′ ∉ H-D^j. O_¬σf satisfies A1, A2 on 𝓗 and 𝓗 satisfies A5, and the O_¬σf-fibre of h is its ≈_{σ, f}-class.
(c) At N = 0, Chg(h) = ∅ for every h.
(d) Constant σ means Chg = ∅, which D-chg^j excludes. Prop 4.1(ii) requires h_v ∈ H-D′ with σ_v constant. ∎

**Lem V3.16 (R-j: what survives).**
- (a) For the base pair with N ≥ 1 and P ≠ V: O(H-D^j ∩ R_B) = O(H-B) = O(H-D^j ∩ H-B) = O(R_B) = {o ∈ O(𝓗) : o ≠ ∅}.
- (b) Prop 4.1(iii) holds for R-j with R4's proof (Lem V2.6(iii); T holds; the D side is not used).
- (c) Every member of H-D^j has Cap containing some iss pair and some adp pair (as in Lem V3.9(d)). So O_¬σf(H-D^j ∩ R_B) ⊊ O_¬σf(H-B) on 𝓗.

*Proof.* (a) The history built in the proof of Lem V3.10(a) has a change at (N, τ) made by a capable, adopted act, so it satisfies D-chg^j and lies in H-D^j ∩ H-B. The rest is as there. (b) Lem V2.6(iii). (c) The Cap claim is the argument of Lem V3.9(d) with D-chg^j's change point in place of B-chg^g's. ⊆: for h ∈ H-D^j ∩ R_B, h[σ ≡ p, f ≡ ∞] ∈ H-B with the same O_¬σf. Strictness: h of (b) of Lem V3.15 made p-quiescent is in H-B with Cap = ∅. ∎

**Rem V3.16a (revision flag).** If R-j were adopted, **R4 would have to be revised**: Prop 4.1(i) generically; Prop 4.1(ii), whose h_v half becomes impossible ("a norm that never changes" is excluded by the class); Lem 4.2 and Cor 4.3; and the parameter condition N ≥ 1. Nothing is revised here.

### 3.11 R-g⁺ (r1, review M2: R-g with its act-existential conjunct)
**Lem V3.17.** H-B^g⁺ ⊆ H-B^g. R-g⁺ satisfies RB1, RB2, M_q^D and N_q, but neither M_p^W nor T. Every statement of Lem V3.9 holds for R-g⁺, and Lem V3.10 holds for R-g⁺.

*Proof.* B-chg^g⁺ implies B-chg^g. The properties are as for R-g (Lem V3.9(a)); N_q holds because q-quiescent histories have Chg = ∅. Lem V3.9(b), (c), (e): every counterexample under R-g is one under R-g⁺, since the scopes (R_B, H-D ∩ R_B) are the same and H-B^g⁺ ⊆ H-B^g. Lem V3.9(d): H-D ∩ H-B^g⁺ ⊆ H-D ∩ H-B^g, so its members have the Cap property; the witness h_b must be changed so that an act enters at N: give a the norm (τ, q), prep 1 and f = N (F1 holds, σ(N)(τ) = q). Then a explains the change at N without capability, w precedes it, Cap = ∅, and h_b ∈ H-B^g⁺. Lem V3.10(a): its history has a entering at N with value σ(N)(τ), so it satisfies the act conjunct. Lem V3.10(b): Lem V2.6(ii-v) needs only M_q^D and N_q. ∎

**Rem V3.17a.** Revision flag: as R-g (Rem V3.10a). R-g⁺ is testable in U and differs from R-g there (`V1B-PREDICTIONS.md`).

### 3.12 R-k (r1, review M3: status- or capability-tied act disjunct)
**Lem V3.18.** Both variants R-k^st and R-k^cap have M, M_q^D and N_q, but not T. On 𝓗 (T = {0, 1}), R4's I₇ is in H-D ∩ R_B, its work event violates, and no h′ as in Prop 4.1(iii) is in H-B^k.

*Proof.* Record clauses and B-conf are 𝐑₀'s. B-chg^k constrains only change points, so it holds on every quiescent history: M_p, M_q^D. N_q through B-conf. *Where T breaks:* I₇ as in Lem V3.12(b): σ′ = (q, p) is forced, with a change at 1; there is no work before 1; a has v = q. R4's added acts are issue acts with prep 1 and no adoption act (fresh additions add no adoption acts), so they are not adopted (R-k^st fails); Cap is unchanged and Cap = ∅ in I₇, so they are not iss-capable (R-k^cap fails). ∎

**Rem V3.18a (REJECTED).** R-k is **REJECTED** as a reading of HYP and is not predicted in V1b. *Reason:* H-B's text says "norms change through norm-making acts" with no status or capability qualifier. Both qualifiers occur only in the H-D list. Reading them into B-chg imports H-D's clauses (D-chg's capability, D-st's status) into H-B, so the reading is not derived from H-B's text, and it narrows the very contrast HYP states. Its formal classification is recorded in Lem V3.18 for completeness.

## 4. Combinations

**Lem V4.1 (r1: relabelled from Rem; interacting combinations).** Readings that replace the **same** clause are not combined.
- **(a)** Among the M-readings R-a, R-b, R-e, R-f, R-h and R-k, every pair that replaces distinct clauses has M, **except R-c = R-b ∘ R-f**, which is not-M (Lem V3.3).
- **(b) R-g ∘ R-f** is not-M. Its S-form counterexamples include every S-form counterexample of R-g and every member of the D-rec class with W = ∅.
- **(c) R-d ∘ R-e.** For the image equalities of (i) under SC1 and SC2 there is no interaction: Lem 3.7's h** has Chg = ∅, and D-chg^e is vacuous there. **The S-form failure set does interact:** the S-form counterexamples of R-d ∘ R-e are S-form counterexamples of R-d, but not conversely; h₁ of Lem V3.6(b) is not a counterexample under R-d ∘ R-e.
- **(d) R-d ∘ R-c.** For the base pair the image equalities of (i) hold. The S-form fails; its counterexamples include R-c's (members of D-rec with W = ∅) and h₁ of Lem V3.6(b).
- **(e) R-a ∘ R-g** (target-tied work-responsive change) needs two targets. **UNTESTABLE IN U.**

*Proof.* (a) The record base of a pair is that of whichever member changes B-rec: R_B, R_B^f = D-rec or R_B^h. RB1 and RB2 hold for each (Lem V2.5, V3.8, V3.11). D-chg^e, B-chg^a, B-chg^k, D-chg, D-st and B-chg are vacuous on quiescent histories (Chg = ∅, f ≡ ∞). Universal B-conf holds on every p-quiescent history. B-conf^b holds on a p-quiescent history iff W ≠ ∅; this is guaranteed on R_B and R_B^h (B-recW) and not on R_B^f (Lem V3.3(a)). So M_p fails only for R-b ∘ R-f.
(b) A member of D-rec with W = ∅: every h′ ≈_{σ, f} has W = ∅ and fails B-chg^g. An R-g counterexample h ∈ R_B: any h′ ≈_{σ, f} h has h's Ref, E and W, so satisfies B-rec, and h′ ∈ H-B^{g∘f} iff h′ ∈ H-B^g. Not-M follows from Lem V3.9(a), whose witness lies in R_B ⊆ D-rec.
(c) H-D^{d∘e} ⊇ H-D⁺ (D-chg ⇒ D-chg^e), so an R-d ∘ R-e counterexample is an R-d counterexample. For h₁: take f*(a) = 1 and σ* = (p, q). F1 holds; the change at 1 is explained by a without capability (D-chg^e); a is adopted at 1 (D-st, D-st⁺); w at 0 conforms; B-chg holds through a; Ref is unchanged. So h₁ has h* ∈ H-D^{d∘e} ∩ H-B.
(d) *Images:* let h ∈ D-rec. If W = ∅, apply (+work) with a fresh unreferenced w₀ (A7; O unchanged, Lem 1.12). Then Cap := ∅ (SC1, SC2 hold for the base pair, R4 Lem 3.7), then σ ≡ p, f ≡ ∞ (Lem 4.0b). The result satisfies D-chg (Chg = ∅), D-st (f ≡ ∞), D-st⁺ (nothing adopted), D-rec (Ref unchanged), B-chg (vacuous), B-conf^b (W ≠ ∅, all conform) and B-rec^c = D-rec, and has observation O(h). The reverse inclusions are as in Lem V2.6(i). *S-form:* an R-c counterexample h has W = ∅ throughout its ≈_{σ, f}-class, so B-conf^b fails there. For h₁, the case analysis of Lem V3.6(b) applies unchanged, because h₁ has a single work event, so B-conf^b and B-conf agree on its class. ∎

## 5. Answer to V1a

**Prop V5.1 (V1a result).** Under R4's hypotheses for each part of Prop 4.1:
- **R-a, R-b, R-e, R-f:** M. D1 (i), (ii) and (iii) hold with R4's proofs (Lem V2.6, Lem V3.1, V3.2, V3.5, V3.8).
- **R-h:** M. (i) and (ii) hold with R4's proofs. (iii) holds only with referenced added acts and A3 (Lem V3.11, V3.12).
- **R-c:** not-M. (ii) and (iii) hold with R4's proofs. (i) **fails** under A1, A2, A5 alone. It holds with A4 and A7 added (Lem V3.3, V3.4).
- **R-d:** not-M. (iii) holds with R4's proof. (i) and (ii) **fail** under A1, A2, A5 alone. They hold under SC1 and SC2 (Lem V3.6, V3.7; R4 Lem 3.7).
- **R-g:** not-M. (i) fails under O_Cap, which satisfies every hypothesis A1–A9 (P ≠ V). (iii) fails. (i) and (ii) hold for (O, 𝓗) when N ≥ 1 and P ≠ V (Lem V3.9, V3.10). (r1) At N = 0 the reading is inconsistent (H-B^g = ∅).
- **(r1) R-i, R-i′:** not-M (RB2 fails). (iii) holds. (i) fails generically (S-form; O₃) and **for the base pair at o = ∅**; on o ≠ ∅ the base-pair images agree (Lem V3.13, V3.14).
- **(r1) R-j:** not-M. (iii) holds. (i) fails generically; (ii)'s h_v half fails for every pair; (i) holds for (O, 𝓗) when N ≥ 1 and P ≠ V; inconsistent at N = 0 (Lem V3.15, V3.16).
- **(r1) R-g⁺:** not-M; as R-g (Lem V3.17).
- **(r1) R-k:** M, not T; (iii) literal fails at I₇ (Lem V3.18). REJECTED as a reading (Rem V3.18a).

*Proof:* collected from the cited lemmas. ∎

**Rem V5.2 (what this means for D1).** Lemma M shows that D1's core survives every reading that is monotone in the sense of M, with the same one-line construction. The non-M readings share one feature: each makes H-B or H-D demand something that the quiescent version of a record-base member lacks: a work event (R-c), a finite entry into force for adopted acts (R-d), a norm change (R-g, R-g⁺, R-j), or (r1) a referenced act (R-i, R-i′). In each case the observation-level non-separation on O can be restored only by spending further freedoms of the frame (A4 and A7; SC1 and SC2; free choice of Cap and work times; (r1) a nonempty record). (r1) By the revision criterion, every non-M reading, and R-h, would require revising R4 if adopted. Whether any is the *intended* reading of HYP is a human decision, not settled here.

**Conj V5.3.** The only HYP-licensed readings under which **D1(i)** fails for the base pair (O, 𝓗) at the R4 parameters with N ≥ 1 and P ≠ V are readings that add a frame-level demand on a coordinate O does not see but the fibre cannot freely supply. *Not established;* stated as a direction for review. (r1) R-i fits this form (the demand is a referenced act; the fibre of o = ∅ has no record to carry it). The conjecture is restricted to (i): R-j's failure of (ii)'s h_v half is not of this form, because there the class contradicts (ii)'s own wording ("a norm that never changes").

In other words, the instrument must be veridical and mapped at least whenever the actual history is in H-B. Nothing in R4 shows that such an instrument exists or does not exist (H14).

And h ∈ H-B. ∎ The witness for S2′ is Lem 3.5(b) with t₁ = 0, t₂ = 1.

477	## 5. Performative ambiguity
478	
479	**Def 5.1.** Let O′ be an observation on a frame 𝓗′, and 𝓒 ⊆ 𝓗′ a class. Identity of records and acts across histories is as in Def 1.7a. A pair (ρ, a) with a an act is **performatively ambiguous in 𝓒 at o** iff there are h₁, h₂ ∈ 𝓒 ∩ O′⁻¹(o) such that:
480	- (ρ, a) ∈ Ref in both h₁ and h₂;
481	- con_{h₁}(a) = ρ, so in h₁ the record *is* the act;
482	- con_{h₂}(a) ≠ ρ, so in h₂ the record *reports* a separate act.
483	
484	A record is performatively ambiguous if some pair containing it is. This is a property of the fibre O′⁻¹(o), not of any one history.
485	
486	**Lem 5.2.** Let (O′, 𝓗′) satisfy A3, A8 and **A9 (no c–con tie)**.
487	- For 𝓒 = 𝓗′ and 𝓒 = H-B′: every pair (ρ, a) ∈ Ref, with a an act, of every h ∈ 𝓒 is performatively ambiguous in 𝓒 at O′(h).
488	- If A1, A2 and A5 also hold, the same is true for 𝓒 = H-D′ and every h ∈ H-D′ ∩ R_B′, and for 𝓒 = H-D′ ∩ H-B′ and every h ∈ H-D′ ∩ H-B′.
489	
490	*Proof* (r2: re-proved; frames are subsets of 𝓗, Def 1.8). Let h be as in the statement, and let (ρ, a) ∈ Ref_h with a ∈ E_h. Since h ∈ 𝓗′ ⊆ 𝓗, h satisfies F2.
491	
492	*The starting history h⁰.* For 𝓒 = 𝓗′ and 𝓒 = H-B′, let h⁰ := h. In the H-D cases, A1, A2 and A5 hold, and h ∈ R_B′ (for the second case because H-B′ ⊆ R_B′). Fix p ∈ P and let h⁰ := h[σ ≡ p, f ≡ ∞]. This replacement satisfies F1 vacuously, so h⁰ ∈ 𝓗′ and O′(h⁰) = O′(h) by Lem 4.0b, and h⁰ ∈ H-D′ ∩ H-B′ by the proof of 4.1(i). In every case:
493	- h⁰ ∈ 𝓒 and O′(h⁰) = O′(h);
494	- h⁰ has the same items, Ref, con, d and r as h, so (ρ, a) ∈ Ref_{h⁰};
495	- h⁰ satisfies F2 (as a member of 𝓗′ ⊆ 𝓗).
496	
497	*Three steps.* Starting from h⁰, build three histories in turn:
498	- **h₂** := h⁰ with con(a) made undefined (h₂ = h⁰ if it is already undefined). F2 imposes no condition on a in h₂. For every other act b, con(b), d(b), Ref and r are those of h⁰, so F2 for b is inherited from h⁰. So h₂ satisfies F2. Only con was changed, so h₂ ∈ 𝓗′ by A9 (applied to h⁰ ∈ 𝓗′), and O′(h₂) = O′(h⁰) by A3;
499	- **h₂′** := h₂ with d(a) := r(ρ). F2 imposes no condition on a, because con(a) is undefined. For every other act b, con(b), d(b), Ref and r are unchanged. So h₂′ satisfies F2. Only d was changed, so h₂′ ∈ 𝓗′ by A9 (applied to h₂ ∈ 𝓗′), and O′(h₂′) = O′(h₂) by A8;
500	- **h₁** := h₂′ with con(a) := ρ. F2 for a holds, because (ρ, a) ∈ Ref (Ref is unchanged throughout) and d(a) = r(ρ). For every other act b nothing relevant changed. So h₁ satisfies F2. Only con was changed, so h₁ ∈ 𝓗′ by A9 (applied to h₂′ ∈ 𝓗′), and O′(h₁) = O′(h₂′) by A3.
501	
502	Hence h₁, h₂ ∈ 𝓗′ ∩ O′⁻¹(O′(h)), (ρ, a) ∈ Ref in both, con_{h₁}(a) = ρ, and con_{h₂}(a) is undefined, so con_{h₂}(a) ≠ ρ.
503	
504	*Class membership.* h₂, h₂′ and h₁ differ from h⁰ only in con and d.
505	- 𝓒 = 𝓗′: shown above.
506	- 𝓒 = H-B′: B-chg, B-conf and B-rec read σ, f, τ, v, the work events with their attributes, and Ref. None of them reads con or d. So h₂, h₂′ and h₁ satisfy them, as h⁰ does.
507	- 𝓒 = H-D′ and 𝓒 = H-D′ ∩ H-B′: h⁰ has σ ≡ p and f ≡ ∞, and the three steps change neither. So Chg = ∅ and D-chg holds; no act enters into force, so D-st is vacuous (Adopted, which reads d, is never invoked); D-rec reads only Ref, which is unchanged. Together with the H-B′ argument, h₂, h₂′ and h₁ are in H-D′ ∩ H-B′.
508	
509	So h₁, h₂ ∈ 𝓒 ∩ O′⁻¹(O′(h)), and (ρ, a) is performatively ambiguous in 𝓒 at O′(h).
510	
511	∎ The countermodels are CM-A3b (O sees con), CM-A8 (O sees d) and CM-A9 (a c–con tie) in §4.4.
512	
513	**Rem 5.2a (what the model does and does not say).** In the model every referenced pair is ambiguous, including a record such as R-56 whose text states its own mode (A10: "a recording note marked not part of the ruling"). That is because the frame has no axiom tying c to con (A9). The relevant condition is this absence of a c–con tie, not A3. Whether real texts do fix the mode is the empirical question of Conj 5.5, which the model does not settle.
514	
515	**Cor 5.3 (the R-A3 convention).** Assume the hypotheses of Lem 5.2. A coding rule that fixes the mode for a class of records, such as R-A3 "act and after-state are the same record" (G04), selects a proper subset of each fibre in which both modes occur. Within the model, that choice is therefore a **convention, not an observation**. *Proof:* By Lem 5.2, each fibre contains both h₁ and h₂ for every referenced pair, and a rule fixing the mode excludes one of them. ∎
516	
517	**Prop 5.4 (relation to D1).**
518	- **(a) Removing the ambiguity does not remove D1.** Let O⁺ = (O, Ref, con, d). No pair is performatively ambiguous under O⁺, because con is seen. Yet O⁺ satisfies A1 and A2, so 4.1(i) and (ii) hold for O⁺ by Lem 4.2. So, in this model, performative ambiguity is **not necessary** for non-identifiability.
519	- **(b) What removing it gives.** Under O⁺, d(a) = r(con(a)) is determined for every constituted act (F2). In H-D, every issue act a in force satisfies f(a) ≥ min{d(b)}, where b ranges over its effective adopters (including a itself when prep(a) = 0); this follows from D-st. If all of these adopters are constituted, recording time becomes a **lower** bound on entry into force. This is consistent with G05, which says recording time is not an *upper* bound. H-B has no such bound: take an act constituted at r = 1, with prep 0 and f = 0. The bound concerns f, which is unobserved (A2), so no separation follows.
520	- **(c) What the ambiguity blocks.** If (ρ, a) is performatively ambiguous in 𝓒 at o and a is an act on τ, then "ρ is independent for τ" (Def 4.9) is **false in h₁**, by its first clause. So it does not hold throughout the fibre 𝓒 ∩ O′⁻¹(o), and O′ cannot certify any such record as independent. (Independence may also fail in h₂, for example when k(ρ) = α(a). Nothing here depends on h₂.) Keeper unobservability (O7) is a **separate**, second obstacle to the same certification.
521	
522	∎ (Each part's proof is given in its statement.)
523	
524	**Rem 5.4a (application to the corpus).** Within R4's model, performative ambiguity does not *explain* the non-identifiability of H-D and H-B (IF's point (ii)). It accounts for a weaker fact: **why the corpus cannot certify one of its own records as an independent observable of the kind Rem 4.9a describes.** Both performative ambiguity and D1 stem from what the observation does not see, but they rest on different unseen coordinates: con and d (with the absence of a c–con tie) for the ambiguity, and σ and f for D1. Applying this to the actual corpus presupposes that the corpus is adequately modelled by (O, 𝓗), which is a modelling choice.

On S_mode it predicts *less* disagreement (the second expected consequence; F-c). r1 stated the conjecture for all register and ruling records, which conflicted with F-c's use of S_mode; that wording is replaced.

541	**Expected consequences, if true:**
542	- disagreement concentrates on records whose text could be either the act or its report;
543	- records whose text cannot itself be a norm-making act show agreement, and records whose text states its own mode (S_mode) show less disagreement than the other register and ruling records (F-c);
544	- any rule that raises agreement does so by stipulating the mode (Cor 5.3). Two different admissible conventions would each be reproducible, yet disagree with each other.

546	**Pre-registration requirement for the falsifiers.** Before any coding for F-a to F-c, the following are fixed and sealed:
547	- the list of record ids forming "the register and ruling records";
548	- the coder pairs;
549	- the set S_mode used by F-c, as a subset of that list;
550	- F-b's review protocol: the reviewers (or the rule selecting them), the reviewer instructions, and F-b's decision rule as stated below (r2, NB-4).
551	
552	**It would be falsified by any of the following.**
553	- **(F-a)** Coders who receive only the texts, with no added mode convention, reach **IF's pre-registered reliability rule, κ ≥ 0.67 for every coder pair** on the field ACT_SELF_PERFORMED, over the sealed list of register and ruling records **outside S_mode**. Cross-family or human coders are especially relevant here; the R2 decision is still pending (F15). This would show that the text does determine the mode.
554	- **(F-b)** A pre-registered independent review classifies the disagreeing cells as coder deviations ("schema admits one answer") rather than "schema admits both". This would point to competence, not ambiguity. **Pre-fixed decision rule (r2, NB-4):**
555	  - *Cells.* Every ACT_SELF_PERFORMED cell, on a record of the sealed list outside S_mode, on which a sealed coder pair disagrees.
556	  - *Who reviews.* Two reviewers. Neither is a coder in any sealed pair, the author of R4, or the reviewer who made IF's exploratory disagreement anatomy. At least one is outside the Claude family or human if the R2 decision (F15) permits; if it does not, this is recorded and F-b is read as within-family. Each reviewer sees the record text, the coding schema and the two codes, but not the coder identities, and classifies without seeing the other reviewer's classification.
557	  - *Classes.* Each reviewer assigns every cell to (a) "schema admits one answer" (a coder deviation) or (c) "schema admits both", the two classes of IF's anatomy.
558	  - *Validity condition.* The two reviewers' agreement on (a)/(c) over all cells reaches κ ≥ 0.67 (IF's threshold). If κ is undefined because both reviewers assign the same single class to every cell, the condition counts as met. If the condition fails, F-b is **undecided** and counts neither for nor against Conj 5.5.
559	  - *Threshold.* A cell is a deviation iff both reviewers assign (a). F-b **falsifies** Conj 5.5 iff, for every sealed coder pair with at least one disagreeing cell, strictly more than half of that pair's disagreeing cells are deviations. Otherwise F-b does not falsify. If no pair has a disagreeing cell, F-b is void, and F-a bears instead.
560	- **(F-c)** For every coder pair, the proportion of disagreements on ACT_SELF_PERFORMED is no lower on S_mode than on the other sealed register and ruling records. S_mode is the set of records whose text states its own mode. Selecting S_mode is itself a mode judgement, so it is made once, before any coding, and not revised afterwards. R-56 (A10, a recording note marked not part of the ruling) is the only such record named in the inputs. A result of F-c is read conditional on the sealed S_mode; a later dispute about S_mode is not evidence for or against Conj 5.5. This would show that the ambiguity explanation does no work. **Power (r2, NB-5): F-c may have no power.** If the sealed S_mode is empty, F-c is void. If S_mode = {R-56}, F-c rests on a single record, and each pair's proportion on S_mode can only be 0 or 1. The inputs also do not establish that R-56 is among the 36 records IF coded. R4 therefore does not claim that F-c can falsify Conj 5.5 with any power; the conjecture's falsifiability rests on F-a and F-b.
